alerts.reason: March net sales fell 0.4% as higher prices and favorable product mix partly offset lower unit sales. Pricing also drove the nine-month sales increase. I forecast that pricing and mix will keep the June quarter above -5% year over year, but that continued unit losses will outweigh those offsets enough for September sales to fall at least 5% (A, B, D).

North America accounted for $339.5 million of $355.7 million in March revenue. Distribution gains supported 37% growth even as the largest distributor reduced inventory days. I expect those gains to keep June revenue growth above -5%, with a September decline of at least 5% if the distributor cuts purchases more sharply as distribution gains slow (A–C).

March revenue fell 3.6% year over year, just 1.4 percentage points above the threshold. Natural gas prices fell 22.3% sequentially. I forecast a June revenue decline still short of 5%, followed by a September decline of at least 5% as weaker gas prices weigh on customer purchases (A, D).

March net sales fell 4.6%. Part of the decline reflected premium pricing in the March 2023 comparison, which supports a June forecast above -5%. Lower customer pricing and deliberate volume cuts at plants undergoing turnarounds could deepen the September decline to at least 5% (A, D).

March net sales rose only 1.7% even as better component availability increased production and helped fill back orders. Backlog fell $49.5 million, or 26.6%, from December. I expect the remaining $136.7 million backlog to support June sales growth above -5%, with fewer orders left to ship in September and a sales decline of at least 5% (A–C).

Cerence accelerated $67.8 million of deferred revenue into its first fiscal quarter, more than the $54.1 million cumulative revenue increase through March. March-quarter revenue was already down 0.8%. I forecast June growth above -5% and a September decline of at least 5%, assuming some of the accelerated revenue would otherwise have been recognized in September (A–C).

Applebee’s domestic same-restaurant sales fell 4.6% in March, and Dine Brands reported lower revenue from both franchise and rental operations. I forecast consolidated revenue growth above -5% in June, followed by a decline of at least 5% in September if restaurant sales weaken further and pull franchise revenue lower (A, B).
